summary.tldr: Requires the health minister to develop and report on a national strategy for universal access to eye care, vision correction and vision aids.
what_it_does: Requires the Minister of Health to work with provinces, Indigenous governing bodies, eye care professionals, patient groups and others to develop a national eye care strategy.

Requires the strategy to identify barriers to eye care and ways to improve access to eye exams, eyeglasses, contact lenses, low-vision aids, surgery and treatment for eye conditions linked to other diseases.
Requires the minister to table the strategy report in both Houses of Parliament within 18 months after the Act comes into force.
Requires the minister to publish the strategy report on the Department of Health website within 10 days after it is tabled.
Requires a second report within five years on the strategy’s effectiveness and the state of access to eye care in Canada, then table and publish it.
who_it_affects: People who need glasses or contact lenses
summary.background: The bill defines an Indigenous governing body as a council, government or other entity authorized to act for an Indigenous group, community or people with rights recognized by section 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982.
